html:
The Battle of the Metaurus was fought in 207 BCE on the Metauro River in the Marche region of eastern Italy. Two Roman armies destroyed a Carthaginian army led by Hasdrubal Barca, the brother of Hannibal.

It was the eleventh year of the Second Punic War. Hannibal was still unbeaten in southern Italy but short of men. Hasdrubal crossed the Alps from Spain with a new army to join him. If the brothers met, Rome would be in great danger. The Romans captured Hasdrubal's letter to Hannibal. The consul Claudius Nero, who was watching Hannibal in the south, secretly took his best troops and marched north for about a week to join the other consul, Livius. Hasdrubal saw he was outnumbered and tried to slip away at night, but lost his way along the river. In the battle Nero led his men around behind the Roman line and struck the Carthaginian flank. Hasdrubal died fighting.

Hannibal learned the news when his brother's head was thrown into his camp. He got no more large reinforcements and withdrew to the toe of Italy. Carthage had lost its last good chance to win the war, which ended at Zama five years later.
